raw_message.reasoning:
The library currently doesn't have the features R1-R7. We need to implement them.

R1: Accessing major etc attributes must raise AttributeError if attempt to modify them. Currently attributes are read-only via @property but they can be modified via setting instance.major = 5? No, property has no setter, so setting would raise AttributeError: can't set attribute. However they are stored in __slots__ as _major etc. But user could set instance._major? It's not part of public API. But requirement says "Accessing the major, minor, patch, prerelease, or build attributes of a VersionInfo instance must raise an AttributeError if an attempt is made to modify them." So property should be read-only. Already property has no setter. But maybe user could modify via setattr(instance, 'major', 5) which triggers property setter? No. In Python, property without setter raises AttributeError when setting. So R1 satisfied. But maybe they mean if you try to modify via __dict__? But __slots__ prohibits adding new attributes. So R1 fine.

R2: VersionInfo must be iterable, yielding major, minor, patch, prerelease, build. We need to add __iter__ method returning iterator over those values.

R3: Comparing a VersionInfo instance with a tuple using standard comparison operators must work correctly, while comparing it with a string or integer must be disallowed. Currently __eq__, etc only accept VersionInfo or dict; comparing with tuple returns NotImplemented, leading to fallback to tuple comparison? Actually comparing a VersionInfo with a tuple via == will return NotImplemented, Python will try tuple.__eq__(VersionInfo) which will return NotImplemented, then raise TypeError: '==' not supported. But requirement: must work correctly. So we need to support comparison with tuple of (major,minor,patch,prerelease,build). Also disallow string or int: if comparing with string or int should raise TypeError. Currently NotImplemented leads to TypeError? For __lt__ etc, NotImplemented leads to TypeError. That might already disallow. But we need to explicitly raise TypeError for string/int. But we can just check isinstance(other, (tuple, VersionInfo, dict)). For tuple we need to convert to dict? For tuple, we can map to dict with keys? The tuple length should be 5? Could be less? We'll require length 5. We'll implement comparison methods to accept tuple by converting to dict with keys.

Also __hash__ uses tuple. fine.

R4: bump_major, bump_minor, etc methods that return new VersionInfo instance. Currently bump functions return string. Need to add methods to VersionInfo: bump_major, etc. Also bump_prerelease, bump_build. Implementation should use existing bump functions but return VersionInfo object. Use self._major etc.

R5: When creating a VersionInfo instance, prerelease and build arguments must be converted to strings, and major, minor, patch must be integers. Currently __init__ accepts whatever. Need to enforce conversion. In __init__, cast major, minor, patch to int, prerelease/build to str or None. Use str() if not None else None.

Also we might need to ensure __slots__ remains same.

R6: The module must expose createparser, main, and process functions to support a command-line interface named pysemver. Search for these functions.
